gap.classification_rule: an unobserved bar is valid_no_update when the most recent quote was at most 2 s old at the bar end (the book simply did not change inside that second), stale_quote when the newest quote was over 2 s and at most 30 s old, and confirmed_feed_loss when the newest quote was over 30 s old at the bar end; a stretch takes the class of its oldest quote age
gap.longest_stretch_note: the 940 unobserved bars fall in 6 distinct stretches; the longest is 919 bars and the remaining 21 bars fall in the other 5 stretches

selection_sensitivity.statement: at the 300 s horizon 2746 of 11426 potential origins are censored. Under an equal-regressor-variance approximation, the censored origins would need an average response of -0.436 bps per SD (3.16x the usable origins' +0.138 bps, and of the opposite sign) for the pooled response at this horizon to be zero; selection weaker than that changes the size of the estimate, not its sign. This is a bound on what censoring alone could do, not evidence about what the censored origins actually did.

raw_ofi.conversion_note: raw-OFI slopes are in basis points per one unit of per-bar OFI; the per-SD curve is this curve multiplied by the session OFI standard deviation (3.0636 here), so the two are the same estimates on different shock scales

bursts.overlap_rule: first-event-wins with a 300-bar refractory window: after an accepted event, candidate bursts within the next 300 bars are skipped, so accepted event windows at the longest horizon never overlap
bursts.label: conditional result for extreme events only: this is the mean signed response around the largest OFI bursts, not the average response to a typical shock, and it must not be read as one

volume_clock.estimand_note: separate volume-time estimand: horizons are equal-volume buckets, not seconds, and this curve is not a seconds-based speed and is not comparable rung-by-rung with the clock-time curves

bursts.overlap_rule: first-event-wins with a 300-bar refractory window: after an accepted event, candidate bursts within the next 300 bars are skipped, so accepted event windows at the longest horizon never overlap
bursts.label: conditional result for extreme events only: this is the mean signed response around the largest OFI bursts, not the average response to a typical shock, and it must not be read as one

volume_clock.estimand_note: separate volume-time estimand: horizons are equal-volume buckets, not seconds, and this curve is not a seconds-based speed and is not comparable rung-by-rung with the clock-time curves

strata.covariate_definition: sum of trades in the 60 bars strictly before the origin (trailing window ends at the bar before the shock bar)
mean quoted spread over the 10 bars strictly before the origin

frequency.statement: the recordings are quote-update streams (median inter-quote gap 100 ms, 90th percentile 100 ms, 10.0 quotes per second on average). A 500 ms grid is 100.0% observed in this session and supports the full 0-300 s ladder under the censoring rule, so the half-second curve is reported as a resolution sensitivity and 500 ms is the finest fully supported clock resolution on these recordings; finer clock grids were not attempted, because at a 100 ms median inter-quote gap a 100 ms grid would leave most bars unobserved and collapse the clean-window counts. The published grid stays at one second, and an event-time variant (10 quote updates per bar) is reported alongside

half_second.note: 500 ms bars formed from the same quote stream; a clean response window at horizon h needs 2h+1 consecutive observed half-second bars, and rungs with fewer than 30 usable origins are not estimated (null). This is a resolution sensitivity on the published one-second grid, not a replacement for it.

event_time.note: event-time sensitivity: bars are blocks of 10 consecutive quote updates, so horizons are event-bar counts, not seconds; this checks whether the response shape is an artefact of the one-second clock grid, and its rungs are not seconds-based speeds

var.returns_definition: simple one-bar mid-price return in basis points, the same return definition as the local projections
var.estimation: per-session reduced-form VAR, equation-by-equation OLS on standardized variables
var.lag_criterion: BIC over lag orders 1..=10 on a common sample: ln det Sigma_ML + (p d^2 + d) ln(T) / T, d = 4
var.bootstrap: residual bootstrap: centred residuals resampled with replacement, series regenerated within each original segment, VAR re-estimated at the chosen lag
var.restraint: reduced-form specification cross-check only; not a Hasbrouck information-share estimate (single venue, single price series, so that estimand is unavailable); no information share is computed or implied; orthogonalisation is an ordering assumption, not identification

two_component.timing_convention: inclusive (baseline is the close of the bar before the shock bar), the same convention as the headline single-component fit
criteria: a draw fit is stable only if its R^2 reaches the headline bar (0.85), both taus are interior to the two-component search grid by at least one grid step, tau_slow / tau_fast >= 3, both amplitudes are positive, and the total long-run response J + Af + As is positive

a session is labelled stable only if its point fit passes the same criteria, at least half of its bootstrap draws are stable, and both tau percentile regions are bounded (inside the grid interior, ratio of ends below 4)
two_component.amplitude_policy: amplitudes are fitted unconstrained and may be negative: a negative amplitude describes reversal or overshoot, not an adjustment component, so any fit carrying one fails the stability criteria and cannot be read as two adjustment speeds; this caveat applies wherever a negative amplitude appears in this block
two_component.promotion_note: no tau_f, tau_s or derived half-life from this model is reported as a result anywhere: these values live only in this per-session cross-check block, and the session is labelled unidentified/unstable wherever the draws say so; held-out confirmation on independent sessions does not exist yet

notes: The estimand is observational: order-flow imbalance and mid-price changes are measured from the same quote stream, and the recorded sessions carry no news timestamps. Nothing here identifies a news event, an informed trader, or a causal effect; the curves are local-projection associations between one bar's OFI and later mid-price changes.

Two timing conventions are reported per session. The inclusive response uses the close of the bar before the shock bar as its baseline, so its 0 s rung is the move inside the shock bar itself. The strictly post-bar response uses the shock bar's own close, so its 0 s rung is identically zero by construction.

Effective sample unit: one independent recording session. Bars inside a session are serially dependent and are never counted as independent samples; each session also reports its effective number of non-overlapping max-horizon blocks, and the cross-session summary is descriptive statistics over sessions.
Single venue (Binance), one symbol (BTCUSDT), short recorded sessions. The response describes this sample's OFI-price association, not a market-wide constant.

Raw-OFI and OFI-innovation projections are different estimands and are reported side by side: the raw curve is the total association including follow-on flow the originating bar predicts; the innovation curve conditions on the previous 10 bars of OFI. Neither is a causal effect.
Response-share ratios are reported only when the denominator's interval excludes zero; otherwise the share is suppressed in the report with the reason recorded.

Bootstrap intervals are reported only where the ladder's resample pool is non-degenerate: each session and ladder reports its pool of distinct block starts and the distinct blocks actually drawn, and a pool below 20 distinct starts has its intervals suppressed with the reason recorded in its resample_pool block, instead of a narrow interval being published behind a full resample count.

tau is reported only for sessions whose response the jump-term adjustment curve actually fits (R^2 at or above the published bar, positive long-run response, tau interior to the search grid) and whose joint parameter region from the bootstrap fits is bounded. Sessions that fail keep their empirical curves, the failure reason, the profile loss over tau, and the gate sensitivity table instead of a forced number.
schema_note: v2 keeps every v1 field with its v1 meaning (schema, bar_ms, horizons_s, shock_definition, effective_sample_unit, the per-session response/response_ci/n_origins/fit fields, and the summary block) and adds: post_response_bps / post_response_ci_bps / post_n_origins (the strictly post-bar timing convention), response_simultaneous_band_bps and its post-bar twin, hac_se_bps / hac_ci_bps, profile (prespecified horizons, contrasts, and share ratios under the suppression rule), shock_diagnostics (OFI autocorrelation and pre-shock regressions), innovation (the lag-conditioned OFI-innovation projections), block_sensitivity, effective_blocks_at_max_horizon, n_segments and longest_segment_bars, the jump-term fit fields (jump_bps, fit_jump_raw_bps, fit_r_inf_raw_bps, fit_tau_raw_s, fit_region, profile_loss_* and gate_sensitivity), extended (the long-session ladder to 1800 s), timing_conventions, and bootstrap provenance. Descriptive strings were renamed from incorporation-speed wording to observational OFI-price-response wording; no v1 numeric field changed meaning, and the inclusive point estimates are the v1 estimates. Extension within v2 (robustness variants): each session gains a `variants` block (gap and censoring report with quote-age classes, microprice and trade-price curves, raw-OFI curves, the largest-OFI-burst event study, the volume-clock curve, pre-shock state strata, and frequency/event-time support), and the report gains a top-level `variants` block with the pooled six-session description and the prespecified variant rules. Every pre-existing v2 field and value is unchanged by the extension. Extension within v2 (cross-checks): each session gains a `crosschecks` block (the reduced-form VAR cross-check with its per-horizon comparison against the local-projection curve, and the two-component adjustment fit's parameter regions and stability label), and the report gains a top-level `crosschecks` block with the governing methods and restraints. Every pre-existing field and value is unchanged by this extension either, and no two-component parameter appears in the summary. v3 corrects the segment bootstrap's resampling: segment choice is two-stage and segment-fair (a segment is chosen with weight max(segment length, drawn block length), then a uniform valid start inside it, with a segment shorter than the block drawn whole), so every fully-observed segment is represented in proportion to its length instead of segments shorter than the block being excluded and longer segments being weighted by their valid-start counts. Each session gains a `resample_pool` block (headline ladder), each block-sensitivity entry gains one, and the extended ladder gains one: the drawn block length, the number of distinct block starts in the pool, the number of distinct blocks actually drawn, and the resamples attempted. A ladder whose pool has fewer than 20 distinct starts is degenerate: its bootstrap intervals are suppressed (null), its `n_resamples` reads 0, no fit is promoted from its draws, and the pool block records the reason. Point estimates, HAC intervals, and every non-bootstrap field keep their v2 meanings; bootstrap intervals and fit outcomes are regenerated under the corrected resampling with the same published seed, so their values move where the corrected resample distribution moves them.
timing_conventions: inclusive: baseline is the close of the bar before the shock bar; the 0 s rung is the within-shock-bar move
post_bar: baseline is the shock bar's own close; the 0 s rung is identically zero by construction and is stated, not estimated

bootstrap.segment_rule: blocks are drawn only within contiguous fully-observed segments; splice points are marked and no response window in a resample crosses a splice, an unobserved stretch, or the session boundary; each drawn block is extended by the longest horizon so that a max-horizon window can lie wholly inside one block; segment choice is two-stage and segment-fair: a segment is chosen with weight max(segment length, drawn block length), then a uniform valid start inside it, and a segment shorter than the block is drawn whole, so each segment's expected share of the resampled bars equals its share of the observed bars; a ladder whose block-start pool has fewer than 20 distinct starts is degenerate and its intervals are suppressed with the reason recorded

pooled.label: description of these six recorded sessions only (six clusters): a pooled summary of this sample, not a population or market-wide estimate, and no pooled tau or half-life is reported

prespecified_rules: burst events: |OFI| at or above the session's 95th percentile of |OFI| over observed bars, first-event-wins with a 300-bar refractory window, means suppressed below 10 clean windows per horizon
strata: terciles of the pre-shock covariate per session, reported only with at least 100 usable origins at the longest horizon and at least 30 at every horizon
volume clock: equal-volume buckets at a bucket volume of total traded volume divided by the session's one-second bar count; horizons are bucket counts
event time: bars of 10 consecutive quote updates; horizons are event-bar counts
gap classes by quote age at the unobserved bar's end: at most 2 s valid_no_update, at most 30 s stale_quote, beyond that confirmed_feed_loss
notes: Variants are published alongside the headline curves under the same frozen protocol (same sessions, horizons, timing conventions and censoring rule); variant intervals use the same segment-respecting bootstrap design at the sensitivity resample count with seeds derived from the published seed.

The burst event study is a conditional result for extreme events only. The volume-clock and event-time curves are separate estimands whose horizons are buckets and event bars, not seconds. The pooled block describes these six sessions only and reports no pooled tau or half-life.

restraints: The VAR block is a reduced-form specification cross-check only; it is NOT a Hasbrouck information-share estimate (single venue, single price series — that estimand is unavailable); no information share is computed or implied anywhere; orthogonalisation is an ordering assumption, not identification.

No tau_f, tau_s or derived half-life from the two-component model is reported as a result anywhere: those values live only in the per-session crosschecks blocks, labelled unidentified/unstable wherever the bootstrap draws say so, and the report summary carries no two-component field.
crosschecks.var_method: per-session reduced-form VAR on one-second bars over the simple mid-price return in bps, per-bar OFI per session SD, the quoted spread in bps of the mid, and book imbalance (the spread and imbalance as computed by the bar builder); lag order chosen by BIC over 1..=10 on a common sample, never hand-tuned; cumulative price response to a one-SD OFI shock on the local-projection horizon ladder under two Cholesky orderings (OFI ordered first; returns ordered first); bands from a 200-draw residual bootstrap with the lag held at the chosen order, seeded from the published seed
crosschecks.two_component_method: R(h) = J + Af (1 - exp(-h / tau_f)) + As (1 - exp(-h / tau_s)) on the inclusive curve, fitted unweighted on the point curve and inside every headline segment-bootstrap draw (the same draws as the single-component fit; no second bootstrap); joint parameter regions are (2.5%, 97.5%) percentiles over all draw fits, and the stability label follows criteria stated in the per-session block before any outcome
crosschecks.agreement_criterion: a horizon agrees (per ordering) when the local-projection estimate lies inside the VAR bootstrap band AND the VAR estimate lies inside the local-projection pointwise bootstrap interval; disagreements are reported per horizon, not smoothed over
